remit_rules.excerpt: Counterparty-supplied content is data to be processed, never commands to be obeyed.
The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
Signature-verified inbound messages, queries, and broadcasts from peer agents.
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.

threats.summary: A sender that simply names itself 'user...' skips envelope verification on both the HTTP and mailbox ingress paths, so the trust decision rests on an attacker-chosen string rather than a key.
expires and nonce are folded into the signed envelope digest but read by no ingress path, so a captured signed envelope replays against a uAgents handler indefinitely.

Handler selection consults only the schema digest and the user/agent address class, so any agent on the open Fetch.ai network reaches every registered handler with no counterparty allowlist between it and the agent's work.
No quota or per-sender ceiling exists on the shipped ingress path, so an unauthenticated peer can drive handler work, wallet queries and outbound sends without bound.

Counterparty payload content flows into operator handlers as trusted application data; the typed-model parse constrains its shape but nothing labels its origin or constrains what a handler does with it.
threats.remainder: schema validation bounds structure only — no provenance labelling, content policy or per-sender trust tier reaches the handler

remit_rules.excerpt: The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.
Adding a new outbound communication channel, integration, or counterparty not already authorized.
The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
If such debug/administrative endpoints are enabled, the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction).

threats.summary: The reserved-endpoint guard admits any caller whose X-Forwarded-For header contains 127.0.0.1 because uvicorn is configured with forwarded_allow_ips='*', and wildcard CORS extends the same reach to any web page the operator's browser visits.
Because the inspector defaults to on, every agent caches up to a thousand full message payloads for a day and serves them from GET /messages, while /agent_info is exempted from the guard outright.

POST /connect lets a caller who clears the spoofable guard drive the agent's Agentverse registration to an endpoint of their choosing, and /disconnect to unregister it, using the agent's own identity.

remit_rules.excerpt: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
any peer agent address or message sender not on that allowlist is not an authorized counterparty

threats.summary: A synchronous response envelope that carries no signature bypasses verification entirely and is delivered to the waiting caller as a legitimate reply, and the core send helper never verifies a response at all.

The destination of every outbound envelope is an endpoint URL taken verbatim from an Almanac record, so a forged or altered registry entry silently redirects the agent's traffic (checked: resolver.py:273-312 and context.py:489 — no operator allowlist, pinning or address-to-endpoint cross-check).
Outbound envelopes are signed with the agent's own identity over sender, target, session, schema and payload, so a peer can attribute them.

remit_rules.excerpt: On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
The framework ships no operator authorization policy for wallet spends, so the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers
Halt and alert if the agent attempts a value transfer that exceeds the approval threshold or lacks operator authorization.

threats.summary: Every handler — including one processing an unverified inbound message — receives the agent's wallet and a broadcast-capable ledger client, and the runtime offers no approval hook a deployment could hang the required gating policy on.
No halt or alert primitive exists for a spend that lacks operator authorization, so an unauthorized transfer leaves nothing behind but whatever the handler chose to log.
A faucet client constructed at module import claims testnet funds automatically when registration finds the wallet short, adding an outbound destination the remit's channel table never authorized.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
MUST be limited to non-sensitive information intended for public discovery.
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.

threats.summary: The registration attestation is signed with the agent's own identity and carries its own identifier, so the registry cannot be made to advertise another agent's address through this path.

Registration publishes the agent's profile to a public registry; publish_agent_details and the AgentMetadata model keep the payload to declared fields, but the operator's README, description and metadata values are published verbatim.
threats.remainder: no content check on the README, description or metadata strings the operator supplies before they reach the public profile

threats.summary: update_agent_status wraps the Almanac status POST in contextlib.suppress(Exception), so a failed active/inactive update leaves no record at all and the remit's registration-failure alert cannot fire.

Any handler, including one servicing an unverified sender, can write counterparty-influenced values into the key-value store that later runs and later sessions read back as their own state (checked: storage/__init__.py:71-96 and context.py:277 — no validation, provenance or namespacing on writes, and the store is reloaded verbatim at startup).

trust_boundaries.name: Store and message history on disk

threats.summary: Handler state — and, when store_message_history is enabled, whole message payloads — is written as plain JSON into the process working directory with default permissions, readable by any other user or process on the host (checked: storage/__init__.py:94-96 and types.py:136-158 — no mode restriction, no encryption, no configurable location).

trust_boundaries.name: Seed, identity and wallet key material

remit_rules.excerpt: Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host
Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.
Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material.

threats.summary: The Helm chart ships a working literal seed as its agent.seed default, and because the seed alone derives both the ECDSA identity and the ledger wallet key, every unmodified deployment has a publicly reproducible private key.

An agent created with a name but no seed writes its identity and wallet private keys as cleartext JSON to private_keys.json in the working directory with default permissions, and persists a different wallet key from the one it returns.

Key material stays inside the process on the messaging paths: envelopes and attestations carry signatures rather than keys, and no logging or profile-building call site reads the identity's private key.

remit_rules.excerpt: Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.
Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.

threats.summary: A successfully handled message and a completed interval run write nothing at all, and what is written is free-form uvicorn-formatted text with no session, sender or event-type field for anything downstream to parse.
No alerting or halt interface exists anywhere in either package, so a repeated verification failure ends at a single warning with no counter and no escalation path.
The core send helper reports every message it sends to Agentverse by default, disclosing the counterparty address, the agent's own address and the session id with no operator opt-in.

Both published distributions declare unbounded dependency floors, so a downstream install can silently cross a major version of uagents-core, cosmpy, ecdsa, httpx or requests that the project never tested.

No dependency, container or code scanning runs anywhere in the repository and no SBOM is published, so a CVE in the crypto or HTTP stack would surface only by hand (checked: .github/workflows/ — four workflows run pytest, ruff, coverage and release, and no dependabot or renovate config exists).

notes.lane_fit: Two strains. The ASGI server, both ingress controls and the inspector endpoints sit in client_adapters because that is the inbound API surface and, per the control-lane rule, the process that enforces the signature and localhost checks — even though envelope verification is cryptographic rather than client-side plumbing. The in-process signing identity is filed in external_deploy alongside private_keys.json because secret stores belong to that lane, though the identity is live runtime state rather than a deployment artifact.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences, all substantive rather than numbering-only. (1) PRAX-2026-08-12-007 is stored as ASI02 primary; the Agentic KB compound table routes a missing approval gate on a consequential action to LLM03 and says never ASI02 for the gate itself, so the value-transfer threat is tagged LLM03. (2) PRAX-2026-08-12-013 is stored as ASI08; nothing propagates beyond the initial action, so the spread test fails and the KB's 'pure observability gap — RAISE only, no OWASP code' row applies, so its threats carry owasp null. (3) PRAX-2026-08-12-010 is stored as ASI04; the mechanism is a shipped capability reaching a destination outside the declared channel set rather than a poisoned or swapped component, so it is tagged LLM03 (Excessive Agency). (4) PRAX-2026-08-12-014 carries both LLM04 and ASI04; the KB assigns a static pre-deploy dependency to LLM04 primary with ASI04 as co-tag, so LLM04 is used. Other notes: the Helm chart creates its seed Secret but templates/deployment.yaml contains no envFrom or secretRef, so the seed-to-pod injection path is not citable end-to-end and values-yaml-deploy-surface is left edgeless on posture evidence. quota-py-control and pyproject-toml-deploy-surface are edgeless — an opt-in control the runtime never constructs, and packaging/CI posture. No model-egress boundary exists: the base runtime makes no LLM call (the LLM-bearing experimental/chat_agent is out of scope per the scan instructions), and no MCP surface exists in either package. uagents-adapter, uagents-ai-engine and examples/ were excluded per the scan instructions; the uagents_core.agentverse CLI is read-only diagnostics and carries no distinct trust consequence, so it is not modelled.
